holdings.thesis: HOLD: 14th consecutive stop-loss review (-22.0% vs. cost basis, $210.97 on 9/25). Rally continued into 9/25 (+8.62% intraday to ~$212.88), extending the 7-day winning streak to ~29% cumulative gain -- moving further from, not toward, the -25% stop-loss threshold. No new company-specific catalyst found in the 9/24-25 window (BofA/Mizuho PT cuts and ECOC conference appearances predate the window); Strong Buy consensus intact. Position ~6.7%.

TRIMMED (sector cap): Tech sector drifted to 30.13% of the portfolio (fractionally over the 30% sector_max_pct cap) on price moves alone. Trimmed DUOL, the largest Tech holding, back to ~29.8% -- a pure sizing rebalance. Fundamentals/thesis unchanged: earnings-growth flag (-27.5% YoY) remains the known deliberate Max-tier sunset/AI-reinvestment story. Insider-selling pattern continues -- SEC EDGAR shows CEO von Ahn Form 4s dated 9/21-22 disposing of ~37,366 shares (~$150-152/share) under his existing 10b5-1 plan; pattern-consistent, no new escalation confirmed in the 9/24-25 window specifically. Position ~11.2% post-trim.

HOLD: no new developments found since 9/24 -- CEO succession to Rahul Singhal remains on track for 9/30; the Hunterbrook/Meta 'Muse' customer speculation (which drove the prior 14.6% jump) is now several days old with no fresh confirmation or denial from either side. Small ~1.7% position -- holding.

HOLD: down -21.6% from cost basis, still short of the -25% stop-loss threshold. Confirmed via 8-K filed 9/24: definitive agreement to acquire King Environmental Services (Europe-based fluid-management/commissioning/load-testing for liquid-cooled data centers), extending EMEA thermal-management reach and building on the 2025 PurgeRite acquisition -- a small, strategically consistent bolt-on, not a negative catalyst. No positive catalyst large enough to move it off the watch list either. Holding without further action.

HOLD: no new antitrust ruling, earnings, or major rating change dated 9/24-25 specifically -- a newly surfaced Buist v. Anthropic AI-industry-coordination suit (naming Google alongside Anthropic/OpenAI/SpaceXAI, filed 9/18) is a watch item but predates this review window. Stock stabilized at $343.92 on 9/24 (+0.46%) after the prior session's antitrust-driven dip. Position ~15.0%, within the trim-tolerance band -- no action needed.

HOLD: the Meta 'Muse' agentic-commerce standoff continued escalating 9/24-25 -- Amazon formally blocked Muse from completing purchases (citing ToS violations), while other major retailers (Walmart, Best Buy, Dick's Sporting Goods) continue embracing Muse instead, a new bearish wrinkle on potential share-of-wallet risk worth continued monitoring. Separately, Amazon opened a new Selling Partner plugin connecting US sellers directly to Claude -- a preferred-AI-partner signal. EU price-parity probe remains live but unescalated. Thesis intact, not yet thesis-breaking.

HOLD: oil-driven move continues -- WTI settled $94.61 on 9/24 (+2.7%) on continued Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz tension headlines; XOM closed $163.52 (+0.6%), outperforming the broader market (Dow -0.3%). No XOM-specific corporate news (earnings, filings, rating changes) found in the 9/24-25 window -- purely macro/oil-price driven. Thesis unchanged.

HOLD: no new catalyst dated 9/24-25 specifically -- stock partially recovered to ~$71.57 on 9/24 after the prior session's 'Muse checkout' concern dip, helped by a Wells Fargo Buy reiteration (9/23). Next earnings confirmed ~Nov 5, 2026. Thesis intact.
HOLD: no rating change or filing found in the 9/24-25 window. Buy consensus unchanged (~35 analysts, ~$269 avg PT); AI-observability demand thesis unchanged.

HOLD: new positive -- signed a research collaboration/license deal with China's InnoCare Pharma (9/24) worth up to $3.35B (~$100M upfront, ~$3.25B milestones) across up to 5 undisclosed targets, an early-stage but incremental pipeline/BD positive alongside the already-known Onswik FDA approval. Shares rose ~2.9-3.7% on 9/24 on the combined news. NAION MDL 3163 litigation: no new docket ruling found in-window; Rule 702 hearing already concluded 9/18, no bellwether trial date set. Obesity/diabetes-franchise thesis intact.

HOLD: only in-window item is routine -- EVP Kelli Keough sold 10,203 shares (~$173K) on 9/21 under a pre-existing 10b5-1 plan (Form 4 filed 9/23), a small scheduled sale, not a red flag. No new update on the Citizens Bank RICO suit or Loop Capital coverage since 9/23. Core digital-bank/fintech thesis unchanged.

HOLD: no new company-specific catalyst -- 9/24 move was macro-driven (broad Dow weakness on rising Treasury yields). Moderate Buy consensus reaffirmed (27 analysts, ~$994 avg PT per MarketBeat as of 9/25). Backlog/AI-datacenter-power-demand thesis unchanged.

HOLD: positive follow-through continues -- confirmed real-time quantum error-correction decoder demo and Superion 256 deployment at Nvidia's Accelerated Quantum Research Center (announced 9/23-24), extending the existing Nvidia partnership (commercial deliveries not expected until 2027, so a narrative/technical catalyst rather than near-term revenue). Shares +4.4% on 9/23 continuing higher into 9/24 on elevated volume, alongside broader quantum-peer strength. FY26 guidance raise and SkyWater acquisition remain the operative thesis.

HOLD, flagging for continued monitoring: touched a fresh 52-week low intraday ($23.72) on 9/24 amid the ongoing sector-wide consumer-credit selloff, before reversing to close near $24.45-24.56 -- a technical breach worth noting given the position is already down ~8%, though no fundamental deterioration accompanies it (no earnings or rating changes in-window; the strong Q2 print -- record $193M contribution profit -- remains the fundamental anchor). Well short of the -25% stop-loss threshold. AI-underwriting thesis unchanged; will recheck closely next review.

HOLD: held its 2026 Annual Meeting on 9/24 (routine proxy vote; one director did not seek re-election, no controversy). The SCAR-program securities class action is old news with its lead-plaintiff deadline already passed. Buy consensus unchanged (~$221 avg PT). Record backlog thesis intact.

HOLD, continuing to flag execution risk: space-sector rally continued 9/24 (+~3-4%, no fresh company-specific catalyst -- sector rotation alongside RKLB/Planet Labs). Additional law-firm class-action solicitation press releases (9/22-24) remain the same known 11/13/26 lead-plaintiff-deadline noise, not a docket escalation. Still-small ~2.0% position -- nothing thesis-breaking.

HOLD: stock +1.99% to $196.95 on 9/24, driven by a hiring announcement (up to 300 new jobs at its Franklin, WI data-center-cooling plant) and continued Data Centers segment momentum (+90% YoY to $348.6M in Q1 FY27 per recent filings). Spinoff mechanics reconfirmed via SEC 8-K/425 (record date 9/28, SpinCo distribution + Gentherm merger close 10/1, rebrand to Modexus Solutions) -- no change from prior thesis. Small position, no action needed.

HOLD: only in-window item is a routine Form 4 -- CFO Neil Laird sold 4,952 shares ($38,328) on 9/24 to cover tax withholding on vested RSUs, retaining 42,246 shares directly; a small, mechanical sale, not a discretionary signal. No new deal/contract news since the Aran Defense/GATE/Bron acquisitions already priced in. Small position, no action needed.

HOLD: strong positive follow-through continues -- confirmed Space Force NITE-STAR contract-vehicle award (up to $981M combined, one of 15 awardees) announced 9/24, shares +5.7% to $74.33. Separately, ARK Invest (Cathie Wood) added ~359,612 shares (~$25.1M) on top of recent purchases, an incremental institutional-buying signal. Small position, no action needed -- continues to validate the thesis.

HOLD: no new company-specific headline dated exactly 9/24-25; nearest catalysts (GEK800 turbofan ignition-test success with GE Aerospace, 9/21; $20M Asia SATCOM gateway contract, 9/1) predate the window but reinforce the existing thesis. FY2026 guidance raise and MACH-TB $1B hypersonics backlog remain the thesis. Newest, least-seasoned position -- continuing to monitor.

HOLD: confirmed 9/24 -- Jodee Kozlak joins as new Chief Administrative Officer effective 9/28, an organizational rather than fundamental development (newly created role overseeing People/Real Estate/Procurement/Corporate Security). No new negative fundamental news found in the 9/24-25 window; Q2 2026 earnings strength and raised FY guidance remain the core thesis. Watching closely on the broadly lower analyst PT trend flagged previously; no action needed yet.

BUY: Satellogic sourced from the 9/23 weekly theme screen (satellite earth-observation/geospatial intelligence). Distinguished from higher-scoring but governance-flagged opportunity-tier candidates on the same screen (RCAT: unresolved CRO retaliation lawsuit plus continued heavy CEO insider selling and a steep downtrend; SERV: FY26 revenue guidance cut from ~$26M to $9-10M plus an explicit risk the core Uber Eats partnership isn't renewed in 2027) by a clean legal/governance profile and Q2 2026 results showing +259% YoY revenue growth and the company's first positive adjusted EBITDA. New concrete catalyst: expanded Slingshot III maritime-domain-awareness contract with the US Office of Naval Research (announced 9/14, six new NewSat Mark VI satellites over 18 months), driving a +3.9% move on 9/25 to ~$6.17. Opportunity-tier (market cap ~$949M); sized to the available cash above the 2% buffer floor (~$12.33), the binding constraint today, funded by today's DUOL sector-cap trim proceeds. Revenue growth off a small absolute base and unproven profitability durability are the key risks to watch.
